item.title: CHAMP Titles: $55 Million Raised To Build Digital Systems For Motor Vehicle Agencies
item.description: CHAMP Titles, a Cleveland-based provider of digital systems for U.S. motor vehicle agencies, announced it raised $55 million in new financing, marking its largest funding round to date and pushing total capital raised to more than $100 million. The post CHAMP Titles: $55 Million Raised To Build Digital Systems For Motor Vehicle Agencies appeared first on Pulse 2.0.

item.title: Biobeat: $50 Million Series B Secured To Expand Commercialization Of Cuff-Less 24-Hour Blood Pressure Monitoring
item.description: Biobeat Technologies announced it has closed a $50 million Series B equity financing to accelerate commercialization of its FDA-cleared, cuff-less 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) system in the United States. The post Biobeat: $50 Million Series B Secured To Expand Commercialization Of Cuff-Less 24-Hour Blood Pressure Monitoring appeared first on Pulse 2.0.

item.title: TransDigm To Buy Stellant Systems For About $960 Million In Cash
item.description: TransDigm Group announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Stellant Systems, Inc., a portfolio company of Arlington Capital Partners, for approximately $960 million in cash, including certain tax benefits. The post TransDigm To Buy Stellant Systems For About $960 Million In Cash appeared first on Pulse 2.0.

item.title: Heron View Partners Launches As Standalone Global Lower Middle Market Private Equity Firm
item.description: Heron View Partners (HVP) has launched as an independent private equity platform backed by Hong Kong-based holding company Pacific Century Group (PCG), following a split from PineBridge Investments after PineBridge’s acquisition by MetLife Investment Management in December 2025. The post Heron View Partners Launches As Standalone Global Lower Middle Market Private Equity Firm appeared first on Pulse 2.0.

item.title: H.I.G. Capital Agrees To Sell Subsea Telecom Provider Xtera
item.description: H.I.G. Capital announced an affiliate has entered into a binding agreement to sell Xtera Limited, a London-headquartered provider of subsea telecom network systems, to a joint venture led by Prysmian S.p.A. and Fincantieri S.p.A. The sale remains subject to regulatory approvals, and completion is expected in the first quarter of 2026. The post H.I.G. Capital Agrees To Sell Subsea Telecom Provider Xtera appeared first on Pulse 2.0.

item.title: Mutares Signs Agreement To Sell Conexus To ATS
item.description: Mutares SE & Co. KGaA has signed an agreement to sell its portfolio company Conexus S.p.A. to ATS – Advance Technologies System S.r.l., a wholly owned subsidiary of Maximum Return System Group, as the firm continues to execute exits from its portfolio. item.title: First Financial Bancorp To Close Acquisition Of BankFinancial
item.description: First Financial Bancorp announced it will close its previously announced all-stock acquisition of Chicago-based BankFinancial Corporation on January 1, 2026, a deal that will give First Financial its first retail consumer-focused locations in the Chicago market. The post First Financial Bancorp To Close Acquisition Of BankFinancial appeared first on Pulse 2.0.

item.title: DigitalBridge And Crestview Partners Complete Take-Private Acquisition Of WideOpenWest
item.description: DigitalBridge Group and Crestview Partners said affiliated investment funds have completed their previously announced take-private acquisition of WideOpenWest (WOW!), a U.S. provider of broadband internet services and connectivity solutions. item.title: Mercantile Bank Completes Merger With Eastern Michigan Financial
item.description: Mercantile Bank announced it has completed its previously announced merger with Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation, combining two Michigan-based financial institutions with a stated focus on serving local households, businesses, and communities. item.title: BriefCatch: $6 Million Series A Raised To Expand AI-Assisted Legal Writing Platform
item.description: BriefCatch, a legal-writing platform used by law firms and courts, has raised $6 million in Series A financing in what the company described as a “significant upround,” as legal organizations accelerate digital adoption while grappling with new risks tied to generative AI.
